title: Glencore receives RIGI approval for Agua Rica (MARA)
gist: Glencore secured Argentina RIGI approval for its MARA copper project (Agua Rica ore processed at Alumbrera), while pulling Alumbrera's restart forward to H2 2027 from H1 2028 as a de-risking bridge. MARA could average over 200kt/yr of copper in its first ten years, and Glencore calls Argentina a key pillar of its copper growth.

insights.claim: Glencore has received approval for its Minera Agua Rica – Alumbrera (MARA) copper project in Catamarca under Argentina's Incentive Regime for Large Investments (RIGI), as announced on 2 October 2026.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Removes a key fiscal/regulatory gating item for a large Glencore copper growth project.
insights.quote: Glencore is pleased to announce that it has received approval for MARA under the Incentive Regime for Large Investments (“RIGI”) in Argentina.

insights.claim: Glencore Argentina's CEO says RIGI provides the fiscal and regulatory certainty required to commit capital at MARA's scale, implying the final investment case depended on the regime.
insights.speaker: Martín Pérez de Solay
insights.so_what: Signals that Argentina's RIGI is effectively unlocking major mining capex decisions, a read-across for other Argentine copper projects.
insights.quote: The RIGI provides the fiscal and regulatory certainty needed to commit capital of this scale

insights.claim: Glencore frames the RIGI approval as a clear sign of confidence in Argentina's long-term investment framework and its ambition to become one of the world's leading copper producers.
insights.speaker: Martín Pérez de Solay
insights.so_what: Major miners publicly endorsing Argentina's investment regime supports the country's emergence as a new copper supply jurisdiction.
insights.quote: a clear sign of confidence in Argentina’s long-term investment framework
insights.locator: RIGI approval is a significant milestone

insights.claim: Glencore has pulled forward first production at the restarted Alumbrera operation in Argentina to H2 2027, from original guidance of H1 2028.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Earlier-than-guided copper volumes from Argentina; a positive execution signal on Glencore's copper growth pipeline.
insights.quote: first production now expected in H2 2027 compared to the original guidance of H1 2028

insights.claim: The Alumbrera restart currently employs close to 2,000 people, mostly drawn from Catamarca province.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Local employment underpins social licence and provincial political support for the project.
insights.quote: The operation is currently providing work for close to 2,000 people

insights.claim: Glencore positions the Alumbrera restart as a de-risking step for MARA: it reduces ramp-up risk for the concentrator and downstream logistics, retains and retrains the workforce before MARA first ore, and keeps critical infrastructure running that will be shared with MARA for operational synergies.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Sequencing a brownfield restart ahead of a large project lowers execution risk and capex intensity versus a greenfield build.
insights.quote: It is designed to reduce ramp-up risk for the concentrator and downstream logistics
insights.locator: The restart is a natural enabler

insights.claim: The Agua Rica deposit in Catamarca has estimated measured and indicated resources of about 1.2 billion tonnes of ore grading 0.47% copper, 0.20 g/t gold, 3.40 g/t silver and 0.03% molybdenum.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Defines a large, long-life polymetallic resource with meaningful by-product credits.
insights.quote: c.1.2 billion tonnes of ore, with average grades of 0.47% copper, 0.20 g/t gold, 3.40 g/t silver and 0.03% molybdenum

insights.claim: MARA plans to process Agua Rica ore at the existing Alumbrera facilities located 35km from the Agua Rica pit, combining the two into one project.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Reusing existing processing infrastructure should lower capital needs and time to production.
insights.quote: The project plans to use the Alumbrera processing facilities, located 35km from the Agua Rica pit

insights.claim: MARA has the potential to produce an average of more than 200,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate per year during its first ten years of operation.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: At >200ktpa, MARA would be a material addition to Glencore's copper output and to global mine supply.
insights.quote: more than 200,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate per annum during its first ten years

insights.claim: Glencore describes Argentina, through the Alumbrera restart, MARA and its plans for El Pachón, as a key pillar of its copper growth strategy.
insights.speaker: Martín Pérez de Solay
insights.so_what: Concentrates a large share of Glencore's copper growth in a single jurisdiction, raising exposure to Argentine policy continuity.
insights.quote: Argentina represents a key pillar of Glencore’s copper growth
insights.locator: Together with the restart of Alumbrera
